descriptionChirho: Architectural term for a 'separate area' or 'separated/restricted space' in Ezekiel's temple vision (Ezek 41:12-15; 42:1,10,13). Refers to the building or open area behind and beside the temple proper that was set apart from the main sanctuary complex. Translated consistently across languages as a demarcated zone: eng: the-separate-area, spa: el-patio-separado, hin: अलग-स्थान, arb: الْمَبْنَى الْمُنْفَصِلِ, kor: 별도의-구역, swa: eneo-lililotengwa.

Noun meaning 'form, figure, shape' referring to the outward appearance or bodily form of a person. Occurs once in Lam 4:7, describing how the Nazirites' form/appearance was more ruddy than coral. This usage is semantically distinct from the architectural term, denoting physical appearance rather than a spatial enclosure: eng: their-form, spa: su-forma, hin: उनका-रूप, arb: صُورَتُهُمْ, kor: 그들-모습, swa: mwonekano-wao.
